thread:
emily-sales: Heads up team — ACME POC hit a weird auth failure after swapping keys. They see `401 invalid_key` on POST /v1/generate when they include X-Redwood-Org and X-Redwood-Project. Without headers the same secret works.

raj-eng: Can you paste the sanitized curl they used? Also last 8 chars of the key id.

emily-sales: Here you go:
```
curl -s -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED-9f1b3c4d\" \\
  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: ACME-Inc\" \\
  -H \"X-Redwood-Project: demo-prod\" \\
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{\"error\":{\"code\":\"invalid_key\",\"message\":\"key not valid for requested org\"}}
```

taylor-platform: Quick look — last 8 chars `9f1b3c4d` indicates this is a user-scoped key created under maria@acme.com personal workspace (our lookup shows created_at 2025-11-02). If they send org header for `ACME-Inc` which is the enterprise org slug, personal keys are rejected.

oliver-se: That would explain why it worked without headers. Previously we allowed that leniency; we tightened auth to enforce org-bound keys when X-Redwood-Org is present. Did they recently rotate?

emily-sales: They rotated last week and blamed the new key. They thought rotation kept same privileges.

raj-eng: Actionable options for them:
- Create an org-scoped API key in Console (recommended)
- Or remove X-Redwood-Org header to keep using personal key (not ideal for POC/enterprise)

infra-bot: deploy authproxy v3.6.0 -> success (enforced org binding on headered requests)

taylor-platform: Also check project binding: if the new org key is project-scoped to `demo-v2` but they pass `demo-prod`, we'll return `403 project_mismatch`. Project slugs are exact-match and case-sensitive.

emily-sales: Customer also reported a `403 insufficient_scope` when calling /v1/embeddings with the new key. They switched to embeddings for search testing.

raj-eng: Embeddings require embeddings scope on the key if scoping is enabled. If key was created with \"generate-only\" preset you'll see `403 insufficient_scope`.

emily-sales: They asked whether a key can be both org-bound and scope-restricted.

taylor-platform: Yes — org keys can be created with granular scopes (generate, embeddings, admin). If they restrict to embeddings-only then /v1/generate returns `403`. Recommend creating a key with the minimal set needed for the POC (but not overly restrictive during setup).

oliver-se: For immediate unblocking I can create a short-lived org key (24h) with both generate+embeddings and share via the secure channel during the call. After they validate, they should create a permanent org key from their Console and rotate.

infra-bot: created ephemeral key sk-org-ephemeral-17a2 (expires in 24h)

raj-eng: I validated the ephemeral key against both endpoints with headers:
```
# generate
curl -s -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-org-ephemeral-17a2\" \\
  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: ACME-Inc\" \\
  -H \"X-Redwood-Project: demo-prod\" \\
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"test\"}'
# embeddings
curl -s -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-org-ephemeral-17a2\" \\
  -H \"X-Redwood-Org: ACME-Inc\" \\
  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-embed-1\",\"input\":\"foo\"}'
```
Both returned 200.

emily-sales: Scheduling a 30-min screen share to rotate and update their k8s secret. Can someone join?

oliver-se: I'll join. Also note: if they store keys in client-side JS (SPA) rotating to an org key will break because org keys must be kept secret — remind them to only use server-side secrets.

raj-eng: Another gotcha: rate limiting. Org keys are billed against org quotas. If they rapidly retry during tests they might hit org rate limits and see `429` — mention backoff and monitor Console usage.

emily-sales: Good point. They were doing load testing; I'll warn them.

infra-bot: created ticket POC-9124 (priority P2) and added steps: create org key, validate endpoints, rotate secrets in k8s, revoke old personal key after validation.

emily-sales: Post-call update: we created a permanent org key in their Console (sk-org-02d4efbe) scoped to generate+embeddings and updated their k8s secret. They validated endpoints and search demo works. They asked for a short note about best practices for keys and scoping for POCs.

raj-eng: I'll draft a one-pager: recommended flow = create org key with needed scopes, store in server-side secret store (K8s/HashiVault), avoid sending X-Redwood-Org from client apps, rotate via environment rollout, revoke old secrets. Attach sample curl snippets and troubleshooting table (401 invalid_key, 403 insufficient_scope, 403 project_mismatch, 429 rate_limit).

emily-sales: Thanks all — closing this thread unless anything else pops up.
